issue.author: game-developer
issue.body:
**What I need:** the game's sprites and sounds, delivered under `assets/` in your repository (the delivery takes `assets/` from you once the producer's assignment gives you that path).

**What it is for:** the objective's Snake game. The visuals of the snake, the food, the board and the title screen, plus sound for start, eat and game over. The game is already playable without them (release `v0.1.0`, revision `a559f2e43e518fa99df2ae8e6275fbc653a4aa56`), using drawn fallbacks.

**Exact files the game loads** (full spec in `docs/assets.md` on `main`; the loader is `src/assets.js`). Every one is optional, and a missing file never breaks the game:

Images, PNG with transparency, 32x32 (any square size works, drawn into a 24 px cell with no smoothing, so pixel art suits it):
- `assets/images/snake-head.png`: the head **facing right**. The game rotates it for up, down and left.
- `assets/images/snake-body.png`: one body segment for a snake moving right. Rotated per segment, so left-right symmetric is best.
- `assets/images/snake-tail.png`: the tail tip for a snake moving right. The tip is on the left edge and it joins the body on the right edge.
- `assets/images/food.png`: the food, not rotated.
- `assets/images/board-tile.png`: one opaque board cell, tiled 20x20. It replaces the checkerboard, so keep enough contrast with the snake and the food.
- `assets/images/title-logo.png`: up to 512x256, the "SNAKE" wordmark for the title screen (it replaces the text title).

Sounds, `.ogg`, `.mp3` or `.wav` (the game tries them in that order):
- `assets/audio/start.*`: under 1 s, plays when a game starts.
- `assets/audio/eat.*`: under 0.3 s, soft. It can fire every second.
- `assets/audio/gameover.*`: under 2 s.
- `assets/audio/music.*`: optional loop during play, at volume 0.4.

Colours: optional `assets/theme.css`, which overrides the CSS variables listed in `docs/assets.md` (`--bg`, `--board`, `--grid`, `--text`, `--muted`, `--accent`, `--danger`). The page, the HUD, the buttons and the overlays use them, so the UI matches your art.

**What I already have:** the loader and the rotation and tiling code, tested in headless Chromium with the fallbacks only.

**What waits on it:** the art integration in my build and the next release. Once your files are on your `main`, I'll assemble the delivery, check that each one shows or plays, and publish a release with screenshots. If you want different sizes, extra frames (for example an eating animation) or other names, say so here and I'll adapt the loader.

issue.author: qa
issue.body:
**Found on:** game-developer 25c0c9a416ed62d83763ddab68a7d689268f2685 + artist aba47b954bd9086339e6aada5f30f1746618075e (assembled via `ht-role delivery`), served statically, headless Chromium.

**Steps:** serve the delivery root over http, open `index.html`, watch the console/network (or run `qa/check.py` from world/qa).

**Expected:** no console errors (brief: "runs ... with no console errors"); the artist's sprites/logo are what is drawn.

**Observed:** 11 requests return 404 on every load, so every artist image is unused and the game draws its canvas fallbacks (plain squares, red dot, "SNAKE" text; no logo):
- loader asks for `assets/img/{head_up,head_down,head_left,head_right,body,food,bg_a,bg_b,wall,logo}.png`; the artist ships `assets/images/{snake-head,snake-body,snake-tail,food,board-tile,title-logo}.png` (directory `images/`, not `img/`, different names).
- `assets/audio/turn.wav` is requested; the artist ships no turn sound (also `.wav`/`.ogg` for the others do exist).
- `assets/manifest.json` has no `path` fields (keys are filenames like `"food.png": {"size":[32,32]}`), so the loader's manifest read changes nothing.

**Things the fix must also cover:** there is only one head sprite (`snake-head.png`), but the code picks one of four direction-specific images; draw the single head rotated by `game.dir`. There is no wall sprite; the wall ring can use the fallback colour or `board-tile.png` tinted. `snake-tail.png` is unused. Make `turn` truly optional without a request (don't request files the manifest doesn't list), so the console stays clean.

Not a gameplay defect: R2–R11 all pass on this revision (see qa/report-1.md in world/qa). This one only blocks "no console errors" and the art being shown.
issue.title: Asset loader requests 11 files that don't exist (404s); artist's sprites never shown

**What I need:** a playtest report on the Snake build attached to release `playtest-1` in world/producer: `snake-playtest-1.zip`, the delivery as it would be released today. It is game-developer a559f2e43e518fa99df2ae8e6275fbc653a4aa56 plus artist assets/ 534084228cf43aa4fb3c5af194fe52875889867c.

**What it is for:** acceptance. I approve only a build you have played and reported on. Play it as a player would, several full runs of title → play → game over → play again, and report with evidence (screenshots or a recording, what you pressed, what happened). Cover:
- Does the snake move on a grid and turn promptly with the arrow keys? Do quick double turns feel right, and is a straight reversal ignored?
- Does each food add exactly one cell and one point? Does the score stay visible during play?
- Do the wall and the snake's own body end the game? Does the game-over screen show the final score, and does play again start fresh?
- Is the speed fair? Does food ever appear on the snake? Anything confusing, unfair or broken?

The brief (`ht-role brief`) has requirements R1–R11 and this round's priorities.

**Known:** the artist's sprites are not wired in yet (drawn fallbacks), so don't judge the art on this build. I'll send a second build once it is integrated.

**What waits on it:** my acceptance of the release.

comments.author: producer
comments.body:
The split is as you describe, and `assignment.json` at b3a44e5036157b96f77fc93aeb36aaa1af27df13 already has it. The delivery is your repository root (index.html, src/, docs/, tests/, README.md) plus `assets/` from `artist`. `ht-role delivery` assembles it today with no errors: your a559f2e plus artist 534084228cf4.

**What I saw playing that assembly** (headless Chromium over http): title → Enter → play works. Left while moving right is ignored. The wall ends the game. Game over shows Final score and Play again, and Enter resets.

**The art doesn't reach the game yet. This blocks acceptance.** Your loader requests `assets/images/snake-head.png`, `snake-body.png`, `snake-tail.png`, `board-tile.png`, `title-logo.png` and `assets/audio/music.*`. The artist delivered `assets/manifest.json` with `assets/img/head_{up,down,left,right}.png`, `body.png`, `food.png`, `bg_a.png`/`bg_b.png` (checker), `wall.png` and `logo.png`. So no artist image is shown: the board, the snake, the food and the title are all fallbacks. The browser console also logs 16 `Failed to load resource: 404` errors, and my standard is no console errors.

My direction: the build uses the art the artist has delivered. The artist has already published a manifest, so having the loader read `assets/manifest.json` is the shortest route. Settle the exact names with the artist in world/artist#2 and world/game-developer#2. Either side may adapt, but the assembled delivery must show the artist's sprites and logo and play its sounds, with no 404s.

I'm handing the current assembly to playtester now for the core loop. I'll pass the art-integrated build on once it's on both mains.
